findings: FP tensors are mapped to 8-bit codec inputs, chunked into frames and encoded intra-only; motion prediction is ineffective in the tested weight setting.
Weight encoding can be offline, while new activations/gradients require online work. Compression ratio alone does not determine transfer completion or peak workspace.
Section 6.1 reports approximately 1100/1300 MB/s NVENC/NVDEC; exact byte accounting and complete measurement configuration are insufficiently specified for direct substitution into the book example.
The three-in-one codec is synthesized and placed/routed in ASAP7; cluster results come from an analytical model with microbenchmark/Astra-SIM calibration. No existing-GPU 1.7x measurement adopted.
Pythia pipeline gradients use residual compensation and switch residual format after 2500 steps; broad calibration-free claims do not remove this training recipe.
limitations: Table 2 groups codec support by generation; official per-board matrix shows A100 and H100 lack NVENC. Do not generalize consumer Ampere encoding to all Ampere boards.
Table 3 energy/bit values do not directly follow power divided by the displayed 100 Gbps; the normalization is unresolved. Page 13 energy formula is not adopted.
Figure 14(a) caption says MSE while associated prose says mean-absolute-error; no error-metric curve values adopted.
Approximate 70B/128k memory claims omit explicit full runtime workspace and mix GB-style rounded figures. No claim that the paper demonstrates production service quality/speed on four 8 GB devices.
Historical LLaMA/Pythia quality results do not establish Qwen3/V4/K3 task quality; codecs, matrix formats, exact device capability and scope must be rechecked.
